description: How MIBiG 3.1 fields correspond to MIBiG 4.0 fields, and how each is normalised before comparison. MIBiG 4.0 restructured the schema entirely -- 3.1 nests everything under a 'cluster' object, 4.0 is flat -- so a raw field-by-field diff reports almost everything as changed. Reconciling the two requires this mapping plus the normalisation rules.

ncbi_tax_id.normalisation_note: 3.1 stores the taxon id as a JSON string, 4.0 as a JSON integer. Compared raw, every shared entry looks changed; compared as strings, only the genuine corrections remain. This is the clearest representation-versus-substance case in the corpus.

locus_accession.normalisation_note: 3.1 has a single loci object, 4.0 a list. The source value counts as present if it appears among the target accessions.

biosynthetic_class.normalisation_note: The two releases use different class vocabularies, so raw sets never agree. Apply class_mapping.json; a source term with no target counterpart is reported as no_counterpart_in_target.

verdict_rules.unchanged: the raw JSON values are equal
verdict_rules.representation_only: the raw values differ but are equal after the field's declared normalisation
verdict_rules.substantive_change: the values differ after normalisation and both are present
verdict_rules.absent_in_source: the source release has no value for this field
verdict_rules.absent_in_target: the target release has no value for this field
verdict_rules.no_counterpart_in_target: a source vocabulary term has no counterpart in the target vocabulary

verdict_precedence_note: Evaluated in this order; the first matching rule applies. Published because a field could otherwise be argued into more than one class -- an absent source value is also trivially 'changed', and a retired vocabulary term is also a substantive change.
